title: Does Marriage Actually Make People Happier
author: Institute for Family Studies
source: Institute for Family Studies Digest, February 25, 2026
summary: IFS research provides compelling evidence that marriage does make people happier, particularly when both partners are committed and engaged. Married adults report higher life satisfaction, greater sense of purpose, and more stable emotional wellbeing than their single counterparts. Yet this data is rarely highlighted in mainstream culture, which often portrays marriage skeptically. The research shows that the happiness gain from marriage is particularly strong for those in committed, stable relationships. This challenges the narrative that individual autonomy and freedom should be prioritized over the bonds of commitment and mutual responsibility.
points: Married people report significantly higher life satisfaction and happiness than single adults.
The happiness gains from marriage are particularly strong in committed, stable relationships.
This research contradicts cultural narratives that prioritize individual autonomy over committed partnerships.
The data suggests marriage provides structure, purpose, and security that contribute to wellbeing.
quotes: Marriage makes people happier—and the numbers prove it.
Married adults report higher life satisfaction, greater purpose, and more stable wellbeing.
Commitment and mutual responsibility, far from constraining happiness, appear to be central to it.” Archived from Institute for Family Studies Digest on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
